newsitem.title: FINLAND: Quotes from Clinton-Yeltsin summit briefing.
newsitem.headline: Quotes from Clinton-Yeltsin summit briefing.

text.p: Here are some key quotes from a news conference given by U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin after their summit ended on Friday:
OVERALL MEETING:
Clinton: "These are dramatic and very substantial results and I'm very pleased with them."

Clinton: "We didn't come here expecting to change each other's mind about our disagreements, but we did come here expecting to find a way of shifting the axis from our disagreements to the goals, the tasks, and the opportunities we share. And we have succeeded."
Clinton: "We have proved once again that we can work together."
Yeltsin: "I would say that emotions sometimes get the upper hand in assessing the Russian-American partnership. This is not the approach that Bill and I have."
Yeltsin: "I firmly believe that we will be able to resolve all issues which, for the time being, are still outstanding. Today's meeting with Bill convinced me of this once again."

Yeltsin: "Finally, we have come to an agreement that this document will be binding for all. And we believe that this document indeed is binding for NATO, for Russia, for all states whose leaders signed this document."
ON NATO ENLARGEMENT:

Clinton: "We are building a new NATO just as the Russian people are building a new Russia. I am determined that Russia will become a respected partner with NATO in making the future for all of Europe peaceful and secure."

Clinton: "I reaffirmed that NATO enlargement in the Madrid summit will proceed and President Yeltsin made it clear that he thinks it's a mistake. But we also have an important and, I believe, overriding agreement."

Yeltsin: "We believe that the eastward expansion of NATO is a mistake and a serious one at that. Nevertherless, in order to minimise the negative consequences for Russia, we decided to sign an agreement with NATO."
ON PLANS FOR START-3 NUCLEAR AND CONVENTIONAL ARMS TALKS:
Clinton: "Now think about it. That within a decade we will have reduced both sides' strategic nuclear arsenals by 80 percent below their Cold War peak of just five years ago."

Clinton: "I think we're doing the right thing, the sensible thing. If it is reassuring to Russia so much the better, we have a clear, new and different mission for NATO in the 21st century but clearly not second-class membership."
Yeltsin: "There's an unprecedented reduction of nuclear weapons, that is of START-3. That is significant."
ON RATIFICATION OF SUMMIT DOCUMENT:
Yeltsin: "As far as Russia is concerned, I expect that the State Duma will make a decision based on my advice."
Clinton: "Boy, I wish I could give that answer."
ON THE ECONOMY:
Clinton: "I am pleased to announce, with the approval of the other G7 nations, that we will substantially increase Russia's role in our annual meeting, now to be called the Summit of the Eight..."
Clinton: "We would be foolish if we walked away from the opportunities that you (Russia) present."

Yeltsin: "...many ... items speak of the fact that the United States has not been that interested in developing a strong economic Russia, or that trade would grow in a healthy way between Russia and the United States. Finally, a breakthrough has been made."

Yeltsin: "I categorically disagree with that formulation that...we sort of bartered here and as a result of that we have come up with these ideas ... This was not a case where we used this as a poker chip."
ON FUTURE U.S.-NATO RELATIONSHIP:
Yeltsin: "The way we solve these issues is by consensus."
Clinton: "A voice but not a veto".
ON HEALTH:
Clinton: "He looks great and he feels great. And I feel fine."
